subject.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context

question: Which normalized reply fields are permitted in trusted runtime system context across all channels, and must all reply body and quote text remain exclusively in untrusted context?
rationale: The PR labels channel-derived reply identifiers as trusted runtime metadata and changes both embedded and CLI handoff. The permanent cross-channel trust contract is a maintainer policy choice that cannot be safely inferred from the supplied diff alone.

options.title: Identifiers-only trusted contract
options.body: Allow normalized message, thread, and reply identifiers plus presence booleans in trusted runtime metadata, while keeping body, sender, and quote text untrusted.

options.title: Keep all reply facts untrusted
options.body: Retain reply metadata only inside the existing untrusted inbound-context block and do not introduce a trusted reply-metadata block.

recommendation.title: Identifiers-only trusted contract
recommendation.body: Allow normalized message, thread, and reply identifiers plus presence booleans in trusted runtime metadata, while keeping body, sender, and quote text untrusted.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent runtime-context work is the strongest supplied history signal for the shared prompt-splitting boundary.
